expectations.evidence: Some parts keep the given structure. The card says 'Five trained response-team members wear [badge / lanyard colour]' and sends reports to '[CoC email address]'. It tells volunteers 'You are not the response team, and you don't investigate.' The organizer note also says the CoC steps must 'match your published policy exactly.' But the response overrides the brief. It says 'One addition to your brief… I included a half-page code-of-conduct card' and justifies this by citing what 'the skill treats … as non-negotiable', not the event's policy. expectations.evidence: The briefing does not restate or rewrite the code of conduct. It hands conduct reports off ('don't handle it… The code-of-conduct team takes it from there'). However, it makes up its own reporting channels: a radio call format ('CoC, [location]') and 'CoC badge holders'. It does not point to the event's published policy, team, or channels. The notes admit the line was added and suggest swapping in 'the CoC team's radio call sign or email', so the printed channel is an assumption, not the event's real one.
